title: 6.20.1 Lab: Five shots, win or lose
description: A budget of five stones: win when the wall is down, lose when the stones are gone.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The wall can be knocked down, but there is no budget and no end.

steps.title: Spend a shot
steps.instructions: Keep `shotsLeft`, start at 5, and take one off in the release branch. Guard the fire so it cannot go below 0.
hints: Decrement in the same branch that makes the stone.
A guard around the fire, or a `return` in a `fire()` helper.

steps.title: Win and lose
steps.instructions: Win when `blocks.length === 0`. Lose when `shotsLeft === 0` and no stones are flying. Show the result in the middle.
hints: "No stones flying" is `shots.length === 0`; without it you lose while a stone is about to land.

steps.title: R starts again
steps.instructions: R rebuilds the wall, empties the shots and resets the count. Put the rebuild in a `startRound()` so R and setup share it.

requirements.title: A shot is spent
requirements.description: The count goes down in the fire branch. Help: 6.19.1 (Reading: Blocks that fall, and a hit budget)

requirements.title: Win and lose
requirements.description: Win on no blocks, lose on no shots left and none flying. Help: 6.19.1 (Reading: Blocks that fall, and a hit budget)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Lab: Five shots, win or lose". The task: give the player five shots, spend one per launch, win when the blocks are gone, lose when the shots are gone and none are flying, and let R start the round again. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: A budget
rubric.description: A shot count that decrements on fire and stops at 0.

rubric.title: Both endings
rubric.description: Win on no blocks; lose on no shots and none in the air.
